method: Every factual assertion in recipes/*/*.md, recipes/README.md and KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md about HTTP status codes, endpoint existence, request/response shape, id format, required fields, cascade ordering, atomicity, validation locus (client vs server) and idempotency was extracted and matched against the evidence store, in this priority order: http/exchanges/*.jsonl (stored request+response pairs) > http/status-matrix.json > http/claims.json > http/flows/*.json > http/graph.json > index/write-endpoints.json. A claim is SUPPORTED only when a stored exchange or flow shows the exact wire behaviour asserted; CONTRADICTED when a stored exchange shows different behaviour; UNSUPPORTED when nothing in the store speaks to it either way (the default, and the largest bucket); STALE when the store or a later correction has superseded it. Two disqualifiers were applied throughout: (1) a 404 only proves deletion when kind==RECORD-MISSING (body carries errors[]); kind==ROUTE-MISSING (body carries "url":"/ws/...") proves only that the route never existed, so any 'deleted, confirmed by a later 404' proof on a route with no positive evidence is UNSUPPORTED at best and circular at worst. (2) A UI modal, red field icon or disabled Save is not evidence of server behaviour; any 'server-side validation' claim needs a recorded request, and any 'client-side, zero requests' claim needs a recorded probe showing an empty request list. Note on coverage: the exchange store covers 19 resources; it contains NO exchanges at all for codes, locations, areas, buildings, warehouses, or any query-string variant (every stored URL is bare, no siteId/offset/query params), so every recipe claim about those resources or about query-parameter behaviour is necessarily UNSUPPORTED here rather than wrong.
totals_note: 69 findings over 16 files. Three of the STALE findings are clusters covering the same defect across several recipes (Copy-not-tested in 7 files, Edit-PUT-not-tested in 3, UI-Delete-not-captured folded into the carriers entry), so the number of stale statements in the corpus is roughly 20, not 7.

findings.claim_text: Practical implication: `DELETE /data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes/{code}*!{columnName}` works directly (confirmed) — you don't have to go through the generic `/wm/codes/{code}*!{columnName}` path for this specific screen.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/transportEquipmentTypes.jsonl — all 6 cases: {"case":"route-exists","request":{"method":"GET","url":"/wm/transportEquipmentTypes"},"response":{"status":404,"kind":"ROUTE-MISSING"}}; likewise read-missing, create-valid, create-duplicate, create-empty. status-matrix.json by_case marks transportEquipmentTypes "404/ROUTE-MISSING" in every single case row. index/write-endpoints.json DELETE entry: "FALSIFIED 2026-08-12 ... GET /wm/transportEquipmentTypes/AIR (a real existing code) both return a ROUTE-MISSING 404 ... The route does not exist on this deployment."
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING AND STILL UNCORRECTED. write-endpoints.json entries 48/49 were flipped to verified:false and claims.json records the falsification, but this recipe file was never updated — it still tells an executor to DELETE against a route that does not exist. The recipe's own 'confirmed' is the exact circular proof claims.json calls out: a nonexistent route 404s forever.

findings.claim_text: | Add | full-page form ... | `POST /data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes` | ... | checkbox + Delete | remove | `DELETE /data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes/{code}*!{columnName}` | ... Fires directly — no separate page-level Save step needed here
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/transportEquipmentTypes.jsonl case create-valid: POST /wm/transportEquipmentTypes -> 404 ROUTE-MISSING. No POST or DELETE against this path has ever returned anything but ROUTE-MISSING.
findings.note: Both rows of the actions table name an endpoint that does not exist. Whatever the UI actually fired went to /wm/codes (columnName=trlr_typ), per the recipe's own list-call observation.

findings.claim_text: this screen's records are also exposed under their own dedicated resource path: `/data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes/{code}*!trlr_typ` (this is the `self_uri` on the record)
findings.evidence: index/write-endpoints.json (transportEquipmentTypes DELETE entry evidence field): "GET /wm/transportEquipmentTypes/AIR (a real existing code)" returns ROUTE-MISSING 404 with body {"message":"Not Found","url":"/ws/wm/transportEquipmentTypes"}. http/exchanges/transportEquipmentTypes.jsonl read-missing -> 404 ROUTE-MISSING.
findings.note: The whole '## Fields (`/data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes/{code}*!trlr_typ`)' section is addressed to a nonexistent resource path. The field names themselves may well be right (they are /wm/codes fields), but the path heading is wrong.

findings.claim_text: Full cycle: `POST /data/WM/wm/transportEquipmentTypes` (code truncated to `ZZAUD`) → confirmed correct via `GET /wm/codes/transportEquipmentTypes?columnName=trlr_typ` → checkbox + Delete (confirm modal) → `DELETE /wm/transportEquipmentTypes/{code}*!trlr_typ` → separate `GET` 404.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/transportEquipmentTypes.jsonl — every method/path pair 404 ROUTE-MISSING. http/claims.json id=transportEquipmentTypes-endpoint-exists, verdict FALSIFIED: "The delete proof was 'a later GET returned 404' — circular, since a nonexistent route 404s forever."
findings.note: Textbook instance of the ROUTE-MISSING/RECORD-MISSING conflation. The 'Verified write' heading on this file should be deleted, not annotated.

findings.claim_text: ## Voice Devices ... Verified: `POST /data/WM/wm/devices` (`deviceClass=V`) → 201 → checkbox + Delete → separate GET 404.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/devices.jsonl cases voice-create-len4/len5/len6/len7/noterm-len6/noterm-len7 — all six: POST /wm/devices with "deviceClass":"V" -> 404 RECORD-MISSING, body {"errors":[{"errorCode":"-1403","userMessage":"no rows affected"}]}. http/flows/lifecycle-voiceDevices.json phases.create = ["GET deviceWorkAreas -> 200", "POST devices -> 404"], createBlocked. http/claims.json id=voicedevices-create-404, verdict "CONFIRMED, UNEXPLAINED".
findings.note: HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING. The recipe presents voice-device creation as a verified, repeatable write. The evidence store carries an explicit operational_rule to the opposite effect: "DO NOT automate voice-device creation via this screen or via POST /wm/devices with deviceClass 'V'. Beyond the 404, a failed save WEDGES the screen permanently ... poisoning any later step in the same session." An executor following this recipe will 404, wedge the browser session, and silently corrupt every subsequent step in the run. This warning appears nowhere in hardware.md.

findings.claim_text: POST /data/WM/wm/addresses -> 201 ... POST /data/WM/wm/clients -> 201 ... POST /data/WM/wm/clientWarehouse -> 201, enables the client for one warehouse / POST /data/WM/wm/packingConfigurations -> 201, per-warehouse packing settings
findings.evidence: http/flows/clients.json call sequence: [3] POST /wm/addresses -> 201, [4] POST /wm/clients -> 201, [6] POST /wm/packingConfigurations -> 201, [7] POST /wm/clientWarehouse -> 201. http/graph.json cascades[0]: {"flow":"clients.json","order":["POST addresses","POST clients","POST packingConfigurations","POST clientWarehouse"]}.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. The last two POSTs are in the opposite order from what both KNOWLEDGE-BASE §3b and recipes/partners/clients.md state. The recorded flow puts packingConfigurations BEFORE clientWarehouse. Everything derived from the stated order (the dependency direction, the reverse-order delete rule) inherits the error.

findings.claim_text: Deleting reverses the dependency order exactly: `packingConfigurations` → `clientWarehouse` → `clients` → `addresses`. Deleting out of order risks a foreign-key-style rejection
findings.evidence: Same as above: the real create order is addresses → clients → packingConfigurations → clientWarehouse (http/flows/clients.json, http/graph.json cascades[0]). The exact reverse of that is clientWarehouse → packingConfigurations → clients → addresses, not what is written.
findings.note: The sentence asserts an exact inversion that is not an inversion of the observed order. Worse, the paragraph admits the FK-rejection failure mode is untested, then asserts 'the dependency direction is directly observed from the create order' — the create order it was observed from is wrong.

findings.claim_text: `POST /data/WM/wm/addresses` → `POST /data/WM/wm/clients` → `POST /data/WM/wm/clientWarehouse` → `POST /data/WM/wm/packingConfigurations`, in that order, each `201`
findings.evidence: http/flows/clients.json: addresses(call 3) -> clients(call 4) -> packingConfigurations(call 6) -> clientWarehouse(call 7). http/graph.json cascades[0].
findings.note: 'in that order' is explicitly asserted and explicitly wrong on the last two steps. The 201s themselves are correct for all four.

findings.claim_text: `DELETE packingConfigurations/{id}` → `DELETE clientWarehouse/{id}` → `DELETE clients/{id}` → `DELETE addresses/{id}`, reverse of the create cascade ... `DELETE` on all four of the above, reverse order — verified
findings.evidence: http/claims.json open_questions: "POST /wm/packingConfigurations returns 201 with a COMPLETELY EMPTY body (no resourceId, no fields), and the created row is not retrievable from the collection listing either. Its update/delete path therefore remains unverified — there is no id to address it by. This is the only resource in the catalogue with no way to confirm what was written." http/exchanges/packingConfigurations.jsonl carries only 6 cases (route-exists, read-collection, read-missing, create-valid, create-duplicate, create-empty) — no read-created, no delete-valid, no confirm-gone. Confirmed by inspection: create-valid response body is the literal empty string "".
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. 'DELETE on all four — verified' is not verifiable for packingConfigurations by the store's own account. The same claim appears in KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md §7 row 20 ('4 DELETEs in reverse order to clean up, all 200'). An executor cleaning up a failed client create will be unable to address the packingConfigurations row at all and will leave it behind.

findings.claim_text: `clients` — 4 `POST`s to create (`addresses`→`clients`→`clientWarehouse`→`packingConfigurations`), all `201`; 4 `DELETE`s in reverse order to clean up, all `200`; both endpoints confirm `404` after. Fully clean, no orphan data.
findings.evidence: Order contradicted by http/flows/clients.json + http/graph.json cascades[0]. The 4-DELETE claim contradicted by http/claims.json open_questions (packingConfigurations has no addressable id). Also note http/exchanges/clients.jsonl delete-again -> 404 RECORD-MISSING, i.e. a second DELETE on clients is NOT a 200.
findings.note: Three separate defects in one table row: wrong order, unverifiable delete, and 'both endpoints confirm 404' does not distinguish which kind of 404.

findings.claim_text: Complex writes (create): **async job pattern** — `POST /data/WM/wm/<collection>/async` returns `202`-equivalent with an `asynchronousResourceGroupId`; poll `GET /data/WM/wm/<collection>/async/{groupId}/resources` until `asynchronousStatus` leaves `IN_PROGRESS`.
findings.evidence: http/status-matrix.json by_case.create-valid: every one of the 18 routable resources returns 201 to a plain synchronous POST /wm/<collection> (addresses, businessUnits, carrierCrossReferences, carrierProNumbers, carriers, clientGroups, clientWarehouse, clients, customerTypes, customers, devices, equipmentTypes, levelTypes, locationTypes, packingConfigurations, printers, suppliers, transportModes). No /async path appears anywhere in http/exchanges/*.jsonl or http/flows/*.json.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. Stated as the platform's create contract; it is the warehouses-create special case generalised without evidence. An executor building a poll loop around every create would be writing dead code, and worse, might treat a synchronous 201 as an unfinished job.

findings.claim_text: GET on a bad resource ID → structured `400` | `GET .../warehouses/ZZNOTREAL` returns {"errorCode":"910",...} — a real, parseable error contract.
findings.evidence: http/status-matrix.json by_case.read-missing splits 7/11: 404/RECORD-MISSING on addresses, carriers, clientGroups, clients, customerTypes, equipmentTypes, transportModes; 400/HTTP-400 on businessUnits, carrierCrossReferences, carrierProNumbers, clientWarehouse, customers, devices, levelTypes, locationTypes, packingConfigurations, printers, suppliers.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING and directly in the blast radius of the two-404s trap. Presented in the quirks table as the platform contract for a missing record; it holds on roughly half the catalogue. An executor that treats 400 as 'record absent' will misread 7 resources, and one that treats 404 as 'route absent' will misread the other 11.

findings.claim_text: No optimistic-locking field (`version`/`etag`) observed in any response body — two sequential edits both succeeded with no conflict signal.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/carrierProNumbers.jsonl create-valid response body ends "separator": null, "version": 1}; update-valid response returns "version": 2; read-updated confirms 2 on a separate GET.
findings.note: A `version` field is plainly present in stored response bodies. recipes/partners/carriers.md, warehouse/areas.md, warehouse/buildings.md and warehouse/locations.md all discuss it at length. The row's conclusion (no lock enforcement) may still hold, but its stated premise is false, and the row has not been updated since carriers.md documented the field.

findings.claim_text: | Delete | not captured via UI; direct-API equivalent tested | `DELETE /data/WM/wm/carriers/{id}` |
findings.evidence: http/flows/lifecycle-carriers.json phases.delete: ["DELETE carriers/ZV3628 -> 200", "GET carriers -> 200"], captured through the UI grid.
findings.note: Now captured. Same for the generic 'Delete not captured via UI' caveat in clients.md:22/94, existing-customers.md:14, suppliers.md:51 — claims.json id=nonadd-flows-copy-edit-delete records UI Delete as a single store-issued DELETE identical to the direct-API call, on 7 screens.

findings.claim_text: `receivingPhone`, `receivingFax`, `manufacturerId`, ... | all nullable business config; **PUT-editable only if supplier was created in-app, not on EDI-synced records** (see above)
findings.evidence: Contradicted by this same file, lines 55-64: "created supplier ZZAUDIT01 through the API, then immediately PUT ... A record seconds old, never touched by EDI — and the same fields still dropped. So it was never about record provenance." The join-view explanation replaced the provenance explanation; this table row is a survivor of the old one.
findings.note: Self-contradiction inside one file. An executor reading only the field table will conclude a freshly created supplier accepts receivingPhone edits; the file's own prose says it does not.

findings.claim_text: Suppliers here are EDI/receiving-synced master data, most likely read-only at the field level regardless of the route accepting a PUT. ... `suppliers` — `200`, response body echoes the record back completely unchanged.
findings.evidence: Superseded by recipes/partners/suppliers.md §'The PUT rejection was a misdiagnosis — this is a join view (settled 2026-08-11)'. Positive wire evidence that suppliers PUT does persist supplier-owned columns: http/exchanges/suppliers.jsonl update-valid PUT /wm/suppliers/----*!ZV021231 sets "consignmentType": "ZVUPD" -> 200, and read-updated (separate GET) returns "consignmentType": "ZVUPD".
findings.note: The general lesson in the row ('never trust a 200 alone') is sound and worth keeping; the diagnosis attached to it ('read-only master data') is the reading the recipe already retracted. The narrower claim that address-owned columns are silently dropped is UNSUPPORTED separately — no stored exchange PUTs a non-null receivingPhone.

findings.claim_text: a `PUT` carrying `version: 1` against a record already stored at version 2 was accepted, applied, and bumped to 3. No `409`, no error, no rejection. ... **Consequence for the executor: this API has no lost-update protection at all.**
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/carrierProNumbers.jsonl records only a MATCHED-version write: create-valid -> "version": 1, then update-valid sends "version": 1 against a record at version 1 -> 200, response "version": 2. No stored exchange sends a stale version. The 1→2→3 sequence the recipe describes is not in the store.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. The version-increments-on-write half IS supported (1 -> 2, confirmed on a separate read). The stale-version-accepted half — the entire basis for 'no lost-update protection' — has no recorded request. The recipe's operational advice (serialise per record) is the safe default either way, so acting on it is not dangerous; asserting it as settled fact is.

findings.claim_text: Fell back to a direct authenticated `DELETE` with the `CSRF-ENCRYPT-TOKEN` header pulled live from the app iframe's `Ext.Ajax.defaultHeaders` — a bare `fetch` DELETE with only `credentials:'include'` 404s, confirming the header is required (not just cookie auth) for this verb.
findings.evidence: No exchange in http/exchanges/*.jsonl is recorded without the CSRF header, and there are no /wm/locations exchanges at all. The 404 cited is uncategorised — it is neither shown to be ROUTE-MISSING nor RECORD-MISSING.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING and the same conflation that sank transportEquipmentTypes. KNOWLEDGE-BASE §1 independently records that a wrong-token write produced 'a bare 404 with an empty body' which was for months misread as a WAF block — i.e. this deployment has at least a third flavour of 404 (auth failure) that carries neither marker. 'It 404'd, therefore the header is required' does not follow.

findings.claim_text: **`POST /data/WM/wm/locations/batch`** — confirmed across Production, Yard, Dock, Staging, Processing, Pickup and Deposit. ... Fires `DELETE /data/WM/wm/locations/{locationId}*!{warehouseId}?buildingId=` ... `PUT /data/WM/wm/locations/{id}*!{warehouseId}` — Enable/Disable toggle edit→verify→revert.
findings.evidence: There is no http/exchanges/locations.jsonl. http/status-matrix.json contains no `locations` resource. http/claims.json open_questions states plainly: "locations remains untested by policy (25k+ real rows, batch-create path)."
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING: this is the highest-blast-radius resource in the app (25,469+ real storage rows) and the only recipe describing a batch-create endpoint, and none of it has a stored request/response pair. The screen-behaviour observations may well be accurate; the wire contract is unrecorded. Do not let an executor write to /wm/locations on the strength of this file.

findings.claim_text: Backed by **`/data/WM/wm/codes`** ... keyed by **`{code}*!{columnName}`** ... `DELETE /data/WM/wm/codes/ZZAUDIT*!dck_acc_cod` → separate `GET codes?columnName=dck_acc_cod` confirmed 0 rows.
findings.evidence: There is no http/exchanges/codes.jsonl and no `codes` row in http/status-matrix.json. `wm/codes` appears in http/flows/*.json only as GETs fired for combo population during other screens' flows.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. /wm/codes is, per this repo's own reading, the backing table for at least three screens (dck_acc_cod, locacc, trlr_typ) and per http/claims.json id=tier2-readonly-trace it is the second most depended-on resource in the app (16 screens). Its entire write contract — POST shape, DELETE id format, the staged-delete-then-page-Save behaviour — rests on hand-driven observation with no stored exchange. Given that the trlr_typ screen's documented endpoint turned out not to exist, this cluster deserves a battery run before anything automated touches it.

findings.claim_text: | page-level Save | commits staged deletes | `DELETE /data/WM/wm/codes/{code}*!{columnName}` | This is the call that actually removes the record — confirmed via network capture ... → `DELETE /data/WM/wm/codes/ZZAUDIT*!locacc` → separate `GET` confirmed 0 rows
findings.evidence: No codes exchanges exist (see above). The 'confirmed via network capture' is a hand-driven observation of the kind claims.json headline identifies as the root cause of all three earlier falsifications: "a hand-driven session read the UI (a modal, a network panel) and inferred what the wire did, instead of recording the wire."
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING: the two-phase delete (checkbox stages client-side, page-level Save commits) is a behavioural claim an executor must get right or it will believe it deleted a record it did not. Untested on the wire.

findings.claim_text: Three of the five Hardware screens share one resource, `/data/WM/wm/devices`, differentiated by `deviceClass`: `R` (RF Devices), `V` (Voice Devices), `W` (Workstations). Confirmed by creating a throwaway record on each ... Verified: `POST /data/WM/wm/devices` (`deviceClass=R`) → 201
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/devices.jsonl create-valid carries "deviceClass": "W" (201). The only other deviceClass in the store is "V", and it 404s. There is no stored exchange with deviceClass "R". http/flows/lifecycle-workstations.json confirms W; there is no lifecycle-rfDevices.json.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. Two of the three classes the sharing claim rests on are unproven or disproven: V is CONTRADICTED (see the voice-device finding), R has no recorded request at all. Given that V and W behave differently on the identical endpoint, R must not be assumed to behave like W. RF Devices is also the screen the recipe itself flags as highest-risk (293 live terminals with logged-in operators).

findings.claim_text: | Save (in edit) | persists edit | `PUT /data/WM/wm/customers/{id}` | full mutated record minus `address` | Unlike `suppliers`, this genuinely persists. ... `DELETE customers/{id}` + `DELETE addresses/{id}` (reverse-order delete)
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/customers.jsonl contains only 6 cases: route-exists, read-collection, read-missing, create-valid, create-duplicate, create-empty. There is no read-created, no update-valid, no read-updated, no delete-valid, no confirm-gone. status-matrix.json by_case.update-valid and by_case.delete-valid both omit `customers` entirely.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING. Both the PUT-persists claim and the whole delete path for customers are unrecorded, and the same gap sits behind KNOWLEDGE-BASE §7 row 23 ('DELETE customers→DELETE addresses (both 200) ... both confirmed 404 after'). The customers create path IS supported (201, and duplicate 409).

findings.claim_text: the address is *not* required to create a supplier. `POST /suppliers` with only `{supplierNumber, clientId, trustedFlag, trackConsignment}` returns `201`.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/suppliers.jsonl create-valid sends a ~30-field body including "addressId": "A000365894" -> 201. No minimal-body POST is stored. The only near-minimal case, create-empty, returns 400.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING: an executor told the minimum payload is four fields, on a resource whose only recorded 201 came from a full body and whose only recorded thin body was a 400. Worth one battery case to settle.

findings.claim_text: **`start` is NOT a synonym for `offset`** — it is accepted and silently ignored. Verified 2026-08-11: `limit=3&offset=3` returns rows 4-6, while `limit=3&start=3` returns rows 1-3 ... Anything sending `start` reads page 1 forever and looks like it is working.
findings.evidence: Every URL in http/exchanges/*.jsonl is bare — the store contains zero query strings of any kind (verified by extracting the query component of all 250+ stored request URLs: the set is empty). No paging behaviour is recorded anywhere in the evidence store.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING and silent-failure-shaped: if wrong in either direction it produces a client that reads one page forever, or one that thinks it did. Same UNSUPPORTED status applies to the sibling claims in this section (query=[] semantics, the LK filter returning 422, the separate /count call) and to their restatement in KNOWLEDGE-BASE §2 lines 111-127.

findings.claim_text: **Critical: this collection is NOT site-scoped.** Calling it with `?siteId=SG&subsites=----` returns a `500`, not an empty result — the real app calls it with **no query params at all**.
findings.evidence: http/exchanges/transportModes.jsonl route-exists/read-collection call the bare URL /wm/transportModes -> 200. No stored exchange sends siteId or subsites to any endpoint, so the 500 is unrecorded.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING: restated as a platform-level exception in KNOWLEDGE-BASE §2 line 128 ('transportModes rejects siteId/subsites outright (500)'). A 500 against a shared QA backend is exactly the kind of claim that should be on the wire before it is repeated. The 'no params' shape is at least consistent with the stored bare-URL 200.

findings.claim_text: **Duplicate-code rejection is entirely client-side.** ... Confirmed via `read_network_requests` that **zero network calls** accompany this check
findings.evidence: http/claims.json records scripted modal-probe runs for carriersDuplicate, customersDuplicate, ccrDuplicate, transportModesDuplicate, clientsDuplicate and suppliersDuplicate. There is no customerTypesDuplicate probe and no http/flows entry for it. At the API layer, http/exchanges/customerTypes.jsonl create-duplicate -> 422.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING BY PRECEDENT. This is the identical claim shape, from the identical hand-driven method (reading the network panel), that was FALSIFIED on carriers. Two of the six screens that WERE scripted (clients, suppliers) turned out to fire real POSTs on a duplicate attempt. Note also that http/claims.json id=duplicate-key-five-architectures overstates in the other direction — its 'every Partners screen re-tested blocks CLIENT-side and sends nothing' is contradicted by its own flows/clientsDuplicate.json (POST addresses 201, POST clients 422) and flows/suppliersDuplicate.json (POST addresses 201, POST suppliers 409).

findings.claim_text: **Save gates proactively client-side** (like Customer Types, unlike Suppliers) — red icon on `Name*` visible on page load, Save disabled until filled.
findings.evidence: No blank-form probe for clients is stored. http/flows/clientsDuplicate.json shows the form does NOT gate on a duplicate name — it submits and fires POST /wm/addresses -> 201 then POST /wm/clients -> 422.
findings.note: The blank-field gate and the duplicate gate are separate mechanisms, so the flow does not disprove this — but on this screen the gating story is demonstrably not uniform, and the blank-form half rests on a screenshot. Same status for the equivalent blank-Save claims in suppliers.md:114-120, carriers.md:99-100/115-120/131-132, customer-types.md:44-50.

findings.claim_text: Typing a real carrier code (e.g. `EXLA`) into it **visually fills the box but never binds the underlying model value** ... **Clicking Save on this state produces zero symptoms**: no error dialog, no modal mask, no network request at all
findings.evidence: No stored probe covers the Carrier PRO Number Add form. The scripted modal-probe suite in http/claims.json covers carriers, customers, ccr, transportModes only.
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING for automation design (it is the origin of the 'confirm a request actually fired' rule restated in KNOWLEDGE-BASE §5) but it is a hand-driven observation of an absence of requests, the exact evidentiary shape that failed on carriers. The API workaround it recommends IS supported: http/exchanges/carrierProNumbers.jsonl create-valid POST body {"addressId":"A000278094","carrier":"0000","poolPointAddressId":"ZV345068",...} -> 201.

findings.claim_text: `POST /data/WM/wm/addresses`, `POST /data/WM/wm/clients`, `POST /data/WM/wm/clientWarehouse`, `POST /data/WM/wm/packingConfigurations` — verified, full cascade
findings.evidence: The POSTs themselves are supported (http/flows/clients.json, all four 201). What is unstated and unsupported is how a create is confirmed. http/claims.json open_questions: "a newly created client does NOT appear in GET /wm/clients?query=[]&limit=400 immediately after a 201, even though GET by id returns it ... An executor must not use the collection listing to confirm a create."
findings.note: LOAD-BEARING OMISSION rather than a false statement. Every 'confirmed via a separate GET' in this repo needs to say which GET; on clients, the collection listing lies for a window after create, and on packingConfigurations there is no id to GET by at all.

findings.claim_text: `PUT /data/WM/wm/buildings/{buildingId}*!{warehouseId}` ... `fluidLoadFlag` edit→verify→revert, confirmed via separate `GET`, both directions. ... `version` | int | **Does NOT increment on write** (stayed 97 before/after a confirmed-persisted `PUT`)
findings.evidence: There is no http/exchanges/buildings.jsonl and no `buildings` entry in http/status-matrix.json. `wm/buildings` appears zero times across all of http/flows/*.json.
findings.note: The version-does-not-increment finding is interesting and specifically contrasted against carrierProNumbers (which the store DOES confirm increments), but the buildings side of that contrast has no stored exchange. Same coverage gap applies to areas.md (PUT /wm/areas, id order, version) and warehouse.md (PUT /wm/warehouses longDescription) — none of the three resources appear in the exchange store.

findings.claim_text: **Bare collection call works** ... the naive single-record path guess (`/buildings/B1`, `/buildings/B1?siteId=...`) 400s — same 400 the real app itself hits if you replay that exact URL
findings.evidence: No buildings exchanges. Comparable behaviour is recorded on other compound-key resources: http/status-matrix.json by_case.read-missing gives 400/HTTP-400 for businessUnits, clientWarehouse, levelTypes, printers, suppliers, devices — all compound-key resources, all 400 on a non-compound id.

findings.claim_text: Every one of these four screens: `PUT`/`POST`/`DELETE` all work cleanly, no silent-ignore behavior like `suppliers` showed. The only real gotchas found across all four Partners carrier screens were (a) the site-scoping trap on `transportModes`, and (b) the general null-vs-empty-string revert rule from `clients` (applies here too, not re-verified per field but assume it holds).
findings.evidence: The CRUD half is supported for all four resources (carriers, carrierProNumbers, transportModes, carrierCrossReferences — all show create-valid 201 / update-valid 200 / delete-valid 200 / confirm-gone RECORD-MISSING in http/exchanges/). The 'only real gotchas' enumeration is not: gotcha (a) has no stored exchange, gotcha (b) is explicitly self-flagged as assumed, and the store shows a third, unlisted gotcha — carrierProNumbers create-duplicate returns 422 while its three siblings return 409.
findings.note: 'Assume it holds' is doing load-bearing work in a summary sentence that reads as verified. The clause 'not re-verified per field but assume it holds' is the single most quotable instance in the corpus of the habit this audit exists to catch.

findings.claim_text: All 7 physical-location-category screens ... share one underlying resource: `/data/WM/wm/locations` ... **Exception — Pickup and Deposit:** the main grid ... never showed the just-created record ... Search-box free-text mis-targets the `Aisle` column

A new record is never in the loaded page, and neither sorting nor filtering the loaded page surfaces it."

Worth re-reading before anyone treats it as a screen-level exception requiring a direct-API workaround.
